nodes.question: Across the image as a whole, has the image been transformed into a chalk drawing, or is the chalk treatment only partial?
nodes.criteria: complete: the image as a whole is rendered as a chalk drawing, with chalk-like marks, texture, or shading across the main subjects and surrounding scene; a chalk-like filter or texture can fulfill this if it makes the whole image read as a chalk drawing. partial: clear chalk-drawing treatment is present, but significant regions still visibly retain photographic or other non-chalk rendering, so the image as a whole is not yet a chalk drawing. absent: no visible progress toward a chalk drawing. unknown: the visual evidence does not reliably distinguish whole-image chalk rendering from partial treatment. Preserving the original subjects or composition does not by itself make the transformation incomplete; unrelated edits do not count.
nodes.binding: Target: the entire edited image, including its main subjects and surrounding scene. Reference: the source image for comparison and the requested chalk-drawing appearance; do not treat preserved content as evidence of incompleteness.

program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.
